note: Baseline for `bun run test`. `units` = tests bun reported SKIPPED per run unit; `failing` = failures PINNED as known, by name. Both are ratchets: any change fails the run and prints what moved. Pin only failures that are understood and filed — never to make a red go away. Seeded 2026-07-27 (v0.2.0 PREP Wave 0).

reasons.novaclaw:server: Windows-from-source. 16 pinned failures. The three PublicApi OpenAPI error-shape tests were removed 2026-08-05 after passing in two independent full runs. The promptAsync entry was stored MOJIBAKED (UTF-8 bytes for an arrow decoded as cp1252), so the ledger could never match its own entry and reported one phantom fix plus one phantom new failure on every run — it was corrected, not removed; that test is still red.

workingSetsNote: Resident WorkingSet64 peak, measured beside the attributed commit peak. Missing units use the explicit UNPROFILED_RESIDENT_MB default; never infer resident demand from commit charge. Core measured 4616 MB resident beside 16552 MB commit across 907 owning ticks on 2026-08-09 (app b2b591b83).
peaksNote: Measured peak MB per run unit — the input to the memory ladder in script/lib/memory-plan.ts. RE-BASELINED WHOLE on 2026-08-07, all twenty at once, from the ATTRIBUTED rows of tmp/peak-series.jsonl. Each entry is the LARGEST attributed reading for that unit across every attributed run (2 to 9 runs per unit); WHOLE_HEADROOM_FACTOR then covers overshoot beyond that maximum. Piecemeal editing is how the dead 1007 MB `core` entry survived four gates, so re-baseline the set or none of it.
peaksScaleNote: 🔴 ROWS ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS 2026-08-07 app 2d6ad8db7. Before it the sampler summed every `bun` on the box by name and every reading also carried the `bun run test` parent shim; after it a sample is attributed by process BIRTH TIME and carries `foreignMb`. No arithmetic converts an old row into a new one — `schema` read 43 (the shim alone, its own process caught by no tick) and reads 552-1236 now. Only rows carrying `foreignMb` were used here. See todo/test-speed.md.
peaksUnsampledNote: TWO units have no entry ON PURPOSE and must not be given one from the series: `script` (largest bound 312 MB) and `effect-drizzle-sqlite` (687 MB). No attributed run of either reached 3 own-ticks — a sub-second unit gets 2-4 ticks at a 200 ms interval, so its recorded max is a LOWER BOUND, and writing a lower bound in as a peak is the bug this whole re-baseline exists to undo. Absent, they plan with UNPROFILED_PEAK_MB (1200), a declared guess that is above every bound observed for them. `schema` is the exception and is listed: it is equally under-sampled, but its largest bound (1236) EXCEEDS that guess, so the guess is falsified and the bound is the safer of the two. Its entry is a floor, not a peak.
peaksLadderNote: Commit and resident demand are planned against independent walls as of 2026-08-09. `core` carries 17958 MB commit and 4616 MB resident profiles; never collapse them through min(free RAM, commit headroom). Sharding core still mitigates little because ~9.3 GB of commit belongs to sixteen bun workers spawned by one flock test file.
